title: Heel-of-Hand Rubbing
summary: The heel of the hand performs short, controlled rubbing movements over larger muscle areas of the back.
goal: Provide more focused work on larger soft-tissue areas while keeping pressure controlled.
imageAlt: Educational diagram of heel-of-hand rubbing without text labels.
startingPosition: The person lies face down. Place the heel of the hand on a muscular area while keeping the fingers relaxed.
instructions: Place the heel of the hand on a soft muscular area.
Use short longitudinal strokes or small circles.
Move gradually instead of staying on one point for too long.
Control pressure with the whole arm rather than only the wrist.
Avoid the spine, scapular borders, and other bony prominences.
direction: Short longitudinal or small circular movements over a broad muscle mass.
tips: Keep the wrist in a neutral position.
Pressure can feel firm but should not be painful.
mistakes: Dropping full body weight onto one point.
Working over ribs or the spine.
Tense fingers and an overloaded wrist.
warning: Do not perform this technique over acute pain, recent injury, significant inflammation, damaged skin, or when touch increases symptoms. Seek qualified professional advice when uncertain.
